113: And if not, they will be unable to walk - There is no route for them on this side, and they are forced to go, on the other (second) bank, for in this situation, against their will, when they go alongside the forest of the non-Jew they walk on the other (second) bank, when they reach alongside me, why would they bother to cross the width of the water, and here they would find it necessary to return and re-cross to the other side when the trimmed part finishes:
